source.title_or_context: **Table 10** Core components of cardiac rehabilitation in frail patients.

table_assessment.assessment_notes: Exact review confirms geriatric/frailty assessment, tailored exercise, monitoring, psychosocial, prehabilitation, nutrition, weight, lipid, and BP instructions. The table mixes non-drug instructions with medication/supplement content, descriptive effect claims, and multiple explicit evidence gaps.

entities.surface_form: evaluation of comorbidities, psycho-cognitive deterioration, physical function, functional capacity, nutritional status, sarcopenia, disability and social deprivation

normative_assertions.notes: MGA including the listed domains should be performed in patients older than 75 years.
Frailty should be evaluated with appropriate tools in patients older than 75 years.

text_units.verbatim_text: MGA should be performed in patients > 75 years including evaluation of comorbidities, psycho-cognitive deterioration, physical function, functional capacity, nutritional status, sarcopenia, disability and social deprivation Frailty should be evaluated with appropriate tools in patients > 75 years

entities.surface_form: Evaluation of frailty as an independent prognostic indicator

normative_assertions.notes: All listed items occur under 'Issues requiring further evidence'.

text_units.verbatim_text: Testing feasibility of MGA in CR environment Standardization of Frailty tool Evaluation of frailty as an independent prognostic indicator

entities.surface_form: Visual and hearing impairments, comorbidities, physical limitations and cognitive status

normative_assertions.notes: Supervised individual activities are listed to prevent or limit disability.
The listed impairments, comorbidities, limitations, and cognitive status must be considered.

text_units.verbatim_text: Supervised individual activities to prevent or limit disabilities. Visual and hearing impairments, comorbidities, physical limitations and cognitive status must be taken into account

entities.surface_form: unable to perform a baseline or cardiopulmonary exercise stress test
a HR slightly lower than that achieved in 6minWT
improving physical capacity and quality of life; reducing disability, frailty level, institutionalization
bed mobilization and postural training or supported walking

normative_assertions.notes: Strength exercise should progress from the specified light-moderate to moderate-high parameters if tolerated.
The row supplies set, duration, rest, frequency, and programme-length parameters.
Aerobic load should be set from 6minWT HR when baseline/cardiopulmonary testing cannot be performed.
These measures are identified for keeping intensity safe and identifying symptoms.
Balance training includes static and dynamic components.
The fragment explicitly labels these as expected outcomes and does not independently direct an act.
Exercise intensity and frequency should be reduced in extremely frail patients.
Some extremely frail patients may only require mobilization/postural training or supported walking.
Progression is explicitly required to be very slow.

text_units.verbatim_text: Strength exercises of 6/8 major muscle groups of upper and lower extremities Exercise starting at light-moderate intensity (30–70% of 1-RM) with 6–8 repetitions, and gradually increased to moderate-high intensity (70–85% 1-RM) and to 12 repetitions, if tolerated and permitted by session time Two to three sets for a total duration of 40–60 min. 5–10 min allowed between different types of exercises and sets. Frequency of sessions 2/3 per week. Length of the programme at least 3–6 months Aerobic training: in many frail patients unable to perform a baseline or cardiopulmonary exercise stress test aerobic training load should be set at a HR slightly lower than that achieved in 6minWT Borg scale and the 'speech rule' are useful to keep resistance or aerobic training intensity within safe limits, in patients able to report symptoms during exercise HR, BP and clinical monitoring are important for identifying symptoms, fatigue or discomfort Balance training includes static and dynamic balance components Expected outcome: improving physical capacity and quality of life; reducing disability, frailty level, institutionalization In extremely frail patients the intensity and frequency of exercises should be reduced. Some of these patients may only require bed mobilization and postural training or supported walking. Progression needs to be very slow

entities.surface_form: long term independence and fall prevention

normative_assertions.notes: The items are under the evidence-gap column, and the balance-training effect is explicitly uncertain.

text_units.verbatim_text: Designing tailored type and intensity of intervention Testing the efficiency of tailored interventions in improving specific outcomes Balance training independent effect on long term independence and fall prevention is still uncertain

entities.surface_form: high quality proteins 15–30 g/day (e.g. whey proteins), essential amino acids 10 g/day or leucine 3 g/day

factual_relations.notes: Supplementation alone is stated to have small effects on sarcopenia/frailty.
When combined with strength/endurance exercise, supplementation can contribute to reduced frailty severity.

normative_assertions.notes: This cell reports effects rather than directing supplementation.

text_units.verbatim_text: Nutritional supplementation alone (high quality proteins 15–30 g/day (e.g. whey proteins), essential amino acids 10 g/day or leucine 3 g/day) has small effects on sarcopenia/frailty, but, if combined with strength and endurance exercise, can contribute to reducing frailty severity

normative_assertions.notes: The role of micronutrients is uncertain and iron-supplementation benefit remains to be evaluated.

text_units.verbatim_text: Role of other micronutrients is uncertain Benefit of iron supplementation is still to be evaluated in frail CR patients with HF

factual_relations.notes: HF patients are stated to be at higher risk of cardiac cachexia.

normative_assertions.notes: The row prioritizes improving sarcopenia over reducing BMI; no narrower allowed operation captures 'improve'.

text_units.verbatim_text: Effort to improve sarcopenia rather than reduce BMI, especially in HF patients at higher risk of cardiac cachexia.

entities.surface_form: associated comorbidities, side effects and reduced life expectancy

normative_assertions.notes: Use of statins should be balanced against the listed risks.

text_units.verbatim_text: Benefit from lipid lowering medication (statins) should be balanced against possible risks from associated comorbidities, side effects and reduced life expectancy

entities.surface_form: patient's clinical status, polypharmacy and frailty
hypotension, fall, electrolyte imbalance, renal failure

normative_assertions.notes: The decision to treat hypertension must consider clinical status, polypharmacy, and frailty.
A personalized approach is advised.
Monitoring is specified for the listed drug-induced complications.

text_units.verbatim_text: Decision to treat hypertension must consider the patient's clinical status, polypharmacy and frailty. A personalized approach is advised with monitoring of drug induced complication (hypotension, fall, electrolyte imbalance, renal failure)

normative_assertions.notes: The benefit is explicitly stated to be uncertain.

text_units.verbatim_text: Whether BP-lowering treatment benefits the very frail patients is still uncertain

normative_assertions.notes: Transition to long-term geriatric centres requires individual evaluation.

text_units.verbatim_text: Transition of care to long-term geriatric centres should be evaluated individually

normative_assertions.notes: Tailored pre-procedure exercise may improve postoperative recovery in frail patients.

text_units.verbatim_text: In frail patients tailored exercise interventions before surgical or invasive procedures may be useful to improve post-operative functional recovery

normative_assertions.notes: Only preliminary studies are stated to be available and standardization remains needed.

text_units.verbatim_text: Preliminary studies available. Standardization is needed
